chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinani, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the twig placed in the grave. He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.الْجَرِيدَة: Twig or small branch, often placed in the grave

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to place a twig in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of placing a twig (*jaridah*) in the grave, reflecting the early Shia acceptance of customary burial rites as a sign of respect and continuity with Prophetic tradition. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating local customs (*urf*) provided they do not contradict core tenets, thereby linking physical acts of remembrance to spiritual dignity.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the twig placed in the grave. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No problem’.
en.sarwar: 9. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Kindiy from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the twig which is placed in the grave. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
